title: HC Mike LaFleur Postgame Press Conference | Week 1 vs. Los Angeles Chargers
headline: Cardinals beat the Chargers in Week 1; Jacoby Brissett got the ball out quickly, Trey McBride scored a TD, and Jeremiyah Love flashed explosiveness in his first game back after weeks without practice.
summary: LaFleur was happy with how the team competed in his first game as head coach, a win. He gave the defense most of the credit and said it looked conditioned enough to play another quarter or two. He took the blame for the offense's red zone problems: a scat call used too much drew a blitz, and he disliked his short-yardage call that had Brissett keeping the ball. He praised Brissett for getting the ball out quickly against pressure, and said clean transitions and drops created hidden yardage on short completions. Kendrick Bourne, Michael Wilson and Trey McBride were part of that efficient passing game, and Marvin Harrison Jr. made a big play against man coverage to get the offense out of a backed-up spot. He said the first touchdown showed explosiveness from a back who hadn't practiced in three or four weeks, and that the backs ground out yards in the fourth quarter. He called the McBride touchdown a mediocre design that good players made work. He flagged three pre-snap penalties, slow huddle exits and the red zone as things to clean up before facing the reigning Super Bowl champions next week.

injuries.detail: Hadn't practiced in roughly 3-4 weeks before the game; LaFleur expects his conditioning and play to keep improving.

signals.claim: Will get better and more conditioned each week and should see a growing workload.
signals.note: He showed explosiveness on the opening TD despite missing weeks of practice, so his role and efficiency should grow as he gets conditioned.
signals.quote: he's just going to get more and more conditioned out there

signals.claim: Remains a key target in the passing game, including a touchdown against Derwin James.
signals.note: LaFleur praised him as a really good, still-young tight end who makes plays even when the design is poor.
signals.quote: they make it right.

signals.claim: Brissett will keep getting the ball out quickly and distributing it in the offense.
signals.note: LaFleur praised his quick release against pressure and his smart decisions, and blamed himself, not Brissett, for the red zone struggles.
signals.quote: I thought Jacoby did a heck of a job getting the ball out.

signals.claim: Harrison had fewer underneath targets but remains the vertical threat against man coverage.
signals.note: His production looked big-play dependent in this game, with fewer short targets than the other receivers.
signals.quote: had the big one versus in man coverage

topics.detail: The offense left a lot of points on the field. LaFleur blamed himself for overusing a scat call that drew a blitz and for a short-yardage call that had Brissett keeping the ball. He said field goals get you beat.

He praised the defense's resilience: it held the Chargers to 13 yards in the first half and 5 in the second, forced turnovers, and pressured the quarterback. He credited the tough training camp for their conditioning.
The offense had three pre-snap penalties and needs to get in and out of the huddle faster. He said he may talk about the penalties too much.
He said the first week is hard for running the ball, but the backs ground out yards in the fourth quarter.

opponent: Reigning Super Bowl champions (team not named in the transcript)

title: Mike LaFleur Press Conference: September 14, 2026
headline: Jeremiyah Love played a monitored but sizable role in his return from injury with no set pitch count, while Mike LaFleur says the two-back looks and Marvin Harrison Jr.'s target count shouldn't be over-read.
summary: LaFleur was pleased overall with the Week 1 win over the Chargers but stressed there is a lot to clean up and that the team must reset quickly. He thought the team got better as the game went on and that the conditioning emphasis from camp paid off, even though the offense looked tired in the first half. He took blame for a poor red zone plan (2-for-5), including a protection and quick-count issue on a play where the Chargers' Derwin James came free, and for a short-yardage call he called horrendous. Jacoby Brissett got strong praise for reading with his feet, getting the ball out, being accurate and making key plays with his legs. Jeremiyah Love was eased back after roughly three to four weeks without practice, with no formal pitch count but monitored snaps. The multiple-back and jumbo personnel groupings were framed as a way to keep defenses guessing, and different backs could fill those roles in other weeks. He cautioned against reading too much into target distribution, including for Marvin Harrison Jr. Josh Sweat is ramping up after a planned light practice load, and Walter Nolen was called disruptive with another level to reach. LaFleur is already several hours into Seattle prep for Sunday at 1:00 and said he will say more on an unspecified situation on Wednesday.

injuries.detail: Coming off an injury and hadn't practiced in about three to four weeks. The staff monitored his snaps in Week 1, and LaFleur called the workload a fair amount.
Has had little practice time, which LaFleur said was scheduled. He is expected to keep ramping up each week.

signals.claim: Love's snap count was monitored but not capped, and his workload should grow as he gets more practice time.
signals.note: His Week 1 volume was limited by the layoff rather than by the game plan, so his role could expand in the coming weeks.
signals.quote: we didn't necessarily have a pitch count per se

signals.claim: Two-back sets with Allgeier and Love were not specifically a pairing, and other backs could fill those looks in other weeks.
signals.note: Allgeier's role in two-back packages isn't locked in and depends on game plan and matchup.
signals.quote: it wasn't really like a Tyler Jeremiah thing.

signals.claim: Knight could be used in the two-back and other personnel packages in future weeks.
signals.note: LaFleur openly likes Knight, so he is a possible rotational or handcuff back to track.
signals.quote: You guys know my love for bam.

signals.claim: Harrison's Week 1 target total isn't a signal of a trend; targets will follow coverages and game flow each week.
signals.note: LaFleur cautioned against reading the target distribution as a fixed pecking order, though he praised a big sideline catch.
signals.quote: I wouldn't look too much into the targets and all that kind of stuff.

signals.claim: McBride's conditioning is fine, and the offense looked less tired in the second half.
signals.note: LaFleur isn't worried about McBride's stamina, and a third-and-three red zone miscommunication with Brissett is being cleaned up.
signals.quote: he looks like he's in great shape

signals.claim: Brissett remains the starting quarterback after a solid, accurate, veteran performance.
signals.note: LaFleur blamed himself for the red zone issues and praised Brissett's footwork, accuracy and sneaks, so the quarterback job looks secure.
signals.quote: I thought he was really solid all day.

signals.claim: Sweat's snaps and practice load will keep increasing week to week.
signals.note: His light practice load was planned, and he should be more involved as he ramps up.
signals.quote: he's just going to continue to ramp up

signals.claim: Nolen drew extra attention in protection and was disruptive, with more room to grow.
signals.note: The positive tone is a good IDP sign for an interior lineman who drew double teams in Week 1.
signals.quote: I thought Walt did some good stuff.

topics.detail: Arizona went 2-for-5 in the red zone. LaFleur said the plan starts with him, pointing to a quick-count and protection issue where Derwin James came free. He added that kicking too many field goals will lose games.
The offense used two-back and 13-personnel jumbo looks so defenses can't focus on one or two tendencies. LaFleur only uses packages the team has practiced.
He stressed camp conditioning in the heat and humidity, noting that the early schedule includes domes and then a hot trip to face the 49ers in two weeks.
He liked the communication process on the fourth-down and kick/punt decisions, which he ultimately makes. He also said he stands by his horrendous short-yardage play call.
Despite the opening win, LaFleur said the team must reset since it is a week-to-week league. He said he will give more information on an unspecified situation on Wednesday.

title: Head Coach Kevin Stefanski Week 2 Media Availability | Monday, September 14th | Press Conference
headline: Stefanski gave no update on QB availability (Penix) for Week 2 vs. Carolina. Lindstrom is in concussion protocol, and Za'Darius Smith, limited to 16 snaps, is expected to ramp up.
summary: Stefanski opened with injury news. A player the captions render as 'DeShawn Hand' has a quad injury that needs surgery and is expected to miss the season. Chris Lindstrom is in concussion protocol, with an update to come later in the week. He called the Week 1 road loss to Pittsburgh frustrating and blamed the minus turnover margin and a series of small mistakes, not just quarterback play. Offensively he pointed to staying on the field: holding penalties, and failed third-and-short conversions. Asked repeatedly about the QB position, including whether Michael (Penix) will be ready, he said he had no update and needed to get through Monday before making any determination. He said Cooper Rush battled, but he wants the turnovers back, and he put the onus on coaches to give players easier completions and a better run game. Za'Darius Smith played only 16 snaps by design, was highly productive (two sacks, three tackles for loss), and will keep being brought along. Bralen Trice played his first pro game, and Stefanski said there is plenty to improve. He backed his kicker, called 'Nick', after a rough game and gave no sign of a change. The next opponent is division rival Carolina at home.

title: Jesse Minter Discusses What He Liked, What He Didn't From Week 1 Tape
headline: Zay Flowers is day-to-day and Ja'Kobi Lane (wrist) could miss longer, opening WR snaps for Devontez Walker and Elijah Sarratt; Minter says Rashod Bateman has 'big days ahead' despite a quiet Week 1.
summary: Minter praised the Week 1 win over the Colts for its physical play in all three phases, including run blocking, downfield blocking by receivers and tight ends, and a swarming defense. On injuries, Zay Flowers is in the day-to-day range and Minter feels good about him, while Ja'Kobi Lane's wrist injury may take longer and is still being evaluated. Minter said there is potential to add a receiver but has confidence in Devontez Walker (who dealt with something minor last week) and Elijah Sarratt, who get a real opportunity. A knee injury to a player the transcript calls T.J. Tampa (not on the roster) could last a week or more and will be clearer this week. The offensive line ran for 200 yards, and first-time starters Jovaughn Gwyn and Olaivavega Ioane drew praise, with some penalties and a Ronnie Stanley chop-block situation to clean up. On defense, Trey Hendrickson had 8-9 pressures and Tavius Robinson had a sack and four QB hits. Marlon Humphrey's forced fumble and Roquan Smith's interception were highlighted. Minter said the red zone defense was his own area to fix. He praised the offense's scheme and its versatility in moving Flowers, Mark Andrews and Derrick Henry around, and previewed a normal game week against the Saints.

title: Joe Brady Talks DJ Moore And Dalton Kincaid's Impact On The Offense
headline: Bills lean on Dalton Kincaid (13 personnel, matchups on every DB) and DJ Moore as defense-warping targets that open looks for Josh Palmer and Khalil Shakir; short week vs. Detroit on Thursday, and 13 personnel isn't guaranteed to return.
summary: Brady said all three phases were not good enough in the win over Houston, citing penalties, a ball put on the ground, and turnover-worthy plays, but praised the team's adjustments and red-zone resilience. He explained that Josh Allen's throw to Josh Palmer came because defenders leaned toward DJ Moore and bracketed Dalton Kincaid, saying Moore and Kincaid 'made the play without making the play' and that this leaves openings for Palmer and Shakir. Kincaid was outstanding in both the run and pass game despite not being 100%, and he was matched up on every defensive back at some point. Buffalo used a lot of 13 personnel (four tight ends) to counter Houston's heavy nickel usage, but Brady stressed it was game-specific, might not recur this week, and the Bills are still feeling out how to use players. He praised the offensive line's competitive stamina against an elite Texans front, though he was frustrated by two sacks and wished the run game had been better. He liked Allen's aggressive style, aside from one late play Allen wants back. Ed Oliver was a captain and received the game ball in an emotional return to Houston. Next up is Detroit on a short Thursday-night turnaround, with Brady saying the 2024 game has no bearing and Detroit has a new defensive coordinator and different personnel.

injuries.detail: Brady said Kincaid is not 100% but still plays at a high level; he missed games last year and trained in the offseason to withstand the workload. Soreness expected for all tight ends after heavy 13 usage.

signals.claim: Kincaid will remain a featured matchup piece in the passing game and stay on the field in both run and pass situations.
signals.note: Brady called him outstanding, said he was matched on every secondary player and Allen trusts him, making him a high-usage TE.
signals.quote: even a banged up Dalton Kincaid when he's out on the football field helps us.

signals.claim: Kincaid is playing through less than full health, and his body is being managed on a short week.
signals.note: Not 100% on a Thursday turnaround; monitor practice reports.
signals.quote: He's not 100% and he's still, you know, playing at a high level.

signals.claim: Defenses will continue to shade safeties toward DJ Moore, creating openings for other receivers.
signals.note: Moore commands attention and made plays including drawing a pass interference penalty, but his gravity also boosts teammates' looks.
signals.quote: obviously DJ made a lot of plays for us yesterday

signals.claim: Palmer will get open looks when defenses bracket Moore and Kincaid, as on the post route from Allen.
signals.note: He is a beneficiary of defensive attention on the top targets, though it's situational.
signals.quote: now if teams are going to double Dalton Kincaid, that leaves a D.J. Moore

signals.claim: Shakir is a go-to option when defenses take away Moore and Kincaid.
signals.note: Mentioned only as part of the group of alternatives; no specific usage change was described.

signals.claim: Allen will continue playing aggressively, taking shots downfield and intermediate throws as the defense allows.
signals.note: Brady said Allen played the style he wanted, supporting a high-volume, aggressive passing approach.
signals.quote: he played the style of game that I wanted him to play.

signals.note: Emotional leadership role as captain and game-ball recipient; Brady referenced a very difficult personal situation, but no fantasy-relevant usage details were given.
signals.quote: no one was deserving more of a game ball than, than at Oliver.

topics.detail: The Bills used four tight ends often against Houston's heavy nickel to gain an advantage, including on the key late crossing route to Kincaid. Brady said it was matchup-based and may not be used this week.
Brady praised the line's competitive stamina against a top defensive front and said pass protection was up to the challenge. He was frustrated by two sacks and wished the run game had been better.
All three phases need cleaner play: too many penalties, a fumble, and turnover-worthy plays. Defensive adjustments after halftime were encouraging, but penalties extended Houston drives.

The Bills face Detroit on a Thursday-night turnaround; staff began preparing for the Lions right after the Houston game. Brady said the 2024 shootout is irrelevant given a new Detroit defensive coordinator and many roster changes.

title: Dave Canales evaluates Week 1 game
headline: Canales called Week 1 the best offense of his tenure: Coker won one-on-ones, Chuba Hubbard set a physical tone, and Bryce Young had command. The defense gave up too many big plays.
summary: Canales said Carolina played hard but not smart. Costly penalties and turnovers, including 17 points off turnovers, sank the team against the Bears. He and the defensive coordinator are asking whether the plan was too much or too little, and he put responsibility on the coaching staff as well as the players. He strongly backed the defensive scheme and said the roster has the pieces to make it work. He blamed the explosive plays allowed, split between runs and passes, on poor front-seven fits, backs reaching the second level, and open-field tackling. On offense he saw the best Week 1 performance of his time in Carolina. He praised Bryce Young's command, play-calling that mixed runs and play action, Jalen Coker winning one-on-one matchups against man coverage, strong tight end play, and Chuba Hubbard's physical running. He was pleased with the offensive line's energy and mostly solid protection, though the Bears' cover-zero pressures hurt at times. Rookie tackle Monroe Freeling bounced back from an early sack and played well in the run and pass game. Canales explained the healthy scratches as a numbers decision, with no room for a fifth tight end on game day.

signals.claim: Young has command of the offense and is extending plays, and the play-calling is creating space for him.
signals.note: The coach's praise of Young's command and play extension supports confidence in the Carolina passing offense going forward.
signals.quote: I saw quarterback have command of the offense.

signals.claim: Coker will keep winning one-on-one matchups, especially against man coverage.
signals.note: Coker had a standout Week 1 against man coverage, which makes him a buy-low or add candidate if defenses keep playing man.
signals.quote: Jalen Coker had a fantastic day of taking advantage of one on one matchups.

signals.claim: Hubbard is the lead back and sets the physical tone for the run game.
signals.note: The coach singled out Hubbard's physical running, which supports his lead-back role and workload.

signals.claim: The offense counts on McMillan in one-on-one situations, including on fourth down.
signals.note: Canales said the offense trusts McMillan in one-on-one situations like the close fourth-and-3 target, which shows how the team views him.
signals.quote: that's one with T-mac one on one. We count on that one.

signals.claim: Freeling settled in after an early sack and played well as a run and pass blocker.
signals.note: A rookie tackle holding up well protects Young and the run game.
signals.quote: I was proud of the way he played.

signals.claim: The team could not dress five tight ends, so a tight end was inactive for special teams numbers.
signals.note: Canales did not name the tight end he meant by "JT", but he said the tight ends played well and that the count of five was too many for the game-day roster.
signals.quote: there wasn't a way to get five tight ends up for the game.

topics.detail: Canales strongly defended the scheme: safeties and the secondary rotate, corners play physically on the edges, and the front seven must funnel runs into alleys. He said the problems were execution and fits, not the system.
The defense gave up many explosive plays, about half runs and half passes. He blamed breakdowns up front and open-field tackling, not a lack of physicality in practice.
Williams hurt Carolina with his legs, including two rushing touchdowns. Canales said containment was poor, the defense must collapse the pocket faster, and defenders need to get off blocks.
Carolina converted around 44% on third down against Chicago's man coverage. The offense mixed runs and play action and handled the cover-zero pressures mostly well.

Canales praised rookies Will Lee, Lee Hunter, Monroe Freeling and Jackson Kuwatch, plus Aaron Hall. Sanders and Cam Jackson were healthy scratches because of the numbers game, with Hunter and Bobby Brown both able to play nose.

title: Ben Johnson after film review of victory over Carolina | Press Conference
headline: Bears ran for nearly 300 yards in the Week 1 win at Carolina. Swift and Monangai (a 60-yard run) both impressed Johnson, and Caleb Williams' scrambling is a bigger part of the offense. Cam Lewis started at safety over Xavier Woods.
summary: Johnson said he was proud of the team for fighting for 60 minutes on the road in hot conditions. Chicago came out of the game in good shape, with only normal bumps and bruises, and no one was ruled out in-game. He praised the run game, crediting the offensive line, tight ends and receivers for explosive runs. He singled out D'Andre Swift for running hard and Kyle Monangai for a 60-yard run. He said the run game is further along than at this point last year. On Caleb Williams, he liked the checkdowns, throwaways and scramble production, and called Williams fast and decisive on his two rushing touchdowns. He said the team may or may not call designed runs for him and may let them happen organically. In the secondary, Jaylon Johnson and Tyrique Stevenson struggled and are expected to bounce back. Rookies Dillon Thieneman (team-leading tackler) and Malik Muhammad got strong reviews. Cam Lewis started at safety after Xavier Woods was worked out that morning and then not made active. Johnson also praised Swift's all-purpose ability and his contract extension. The next opponent is the division rival Minnesota Vikings at home.

injuries.detail: Worked out the morning of the game, but the team decided to make Cam Lewis active and start him at safety instead. The nature of the issue wasn't specified.

signals.note: Johnson called him a huge part of the offense and an all-purpose back, not just a scatback, which supports a high-volume role.
signals.quote: he's really an all purpose back as far as I'm concerned.

signals.note: The explosive run and the checkdown work show he has a real role alongside Swift.
signals.quote: It was good to see him break out a 60 yarder and run really hard

signals.claim: Williams' scrambling and his designed or organic rushing will remain part of the offense, though designed runs aren't guaranteed.
signals.note: His rushing upside, including two rushing TDs, boosts his fantasy floor and ceiling; Johnson said the team may or may not call designed runs.
signals.quote: He was decisive. Uh, he's really fast.

signals.note: For IDP and defense-streaming purposes, the coach praised his debut and coverage.

signals.claim: Lewis started at safety after Xavier Woods was not made active, and played really well.
signals.note: His future role depends on Woods' availability, which is a small IDP watch item.

signals.note: A rebound is expected, but he had coverage issues in Week 1, which matters for the Bears' defense.
signals.quote: they'll bounce back no problem.

signals.claim: Stevenson is expected to bounce back after a rough coverage game.
signals.note: He had coverage issues in Week 1, and the coach said both players felt they could play better.
signals.quote: this team needs them so they'll bounce back no problem.

topics.detail: The Bears rushed for nearly 300 yards. Johnson credited the offensive line, tight ends and receivers, and said the run game is ahead of where it was a year ago. He referenced the 'no block, no rock' idea.
The team had 12 penalties in the game, and Johnson said they don't want them.
The team came out in pretty good shape with only normal bumps and bruises, and they will see how things look through the week.

Johnson liked Williams' checkdowns, resets to the middle of the field, throwaways and scramble production. He relayed Drew Brees's advice that the difference between 60% and 70% completions is about three completions per game.

title: Zac Taylor Recaps Week 1 Victory over Buccaneers | PRESS CONFERENCE
headline: Dohnte Meyers earned praise for two space plays and a possible return role, Tee Higgins made a big contested catch, and Chase Brown had big holes behind a line that kept Burrow clean.
summary: Taylor was happy with the Week 1 win over Tampa Bay, in which Cincinnati led 21-3 at one point, and said the goal is to be the best team at the end of the season, not in Week 1. He praised Dexter Lawrence's impact, noting that it shows up in the production of the players around him. He liked how quickly Barrett Carter and Demetrius Knight diagnosed plays, with Carter wearing the headset and getting the defense into the right calls. The offensive line got high marks for keeping Joe Burrow clean and opening big holes for Chase Brown. Taylor singled out Dohnte Meyers for two space plays on the closing drive, a jet sweep and the drive starter, and for his ball security. He said the team wants to get the ball to Ja'Marr Chase, but other players have to make plays when their number is called. He called Burrow's throw to Tee Higgins very impressive, and said he isn't concerned about Burrow's pick-six. He was unhappy with four offside penalties spread across multiple defenders, and said tackling was good for Week 1. Houston is next.

signals.claim: Lawrence will keep drawing extra attention that creates production for teammates.
signals.note: Lawrence's value may show up as pressure and run disruption rather than raw stats, which helps the players around him, including IDP leagues.
signals.quote: he still was in there and made his presence felt

signals.claim: Carter will keep wearing the headset and making the defensive calls.
signals.note: Playcalling and command of the defense point to a secure, high-snap role for an IDP linebacker.
signals.quote: doing a great job getting us in the right calls

signals.claim: Knight will keep playing as a starting linebacker alongside Carter.
signals.note: Taylor praised his quick diagnosis, which supports steady snaps and tackle volume for IDP.
signals.quote: there's no hesitation

signals.claim: Brown will keep getting the lead carries behind a line that opened big holes.

title: Todd Monken Press Conference : September 14th, 2026
headline: Monken says Deshaun Watson will start vs. Tampa Bay after a rough Week 2 loss to Jacksonville; Dylan Sampson's status is still being evaluated, and rookie OL Austin Barber is expected to start.
summary: Monken called the loss to Jacksonville disappointing. He said effort and physicality were fine, but the operation, communication and 'Browns hurting Browns' mistakes were below the line. After watching the tape he anticipates Deshaun Watson will start at Tampa Bay. He said the film confirmed that decision and that the offense has to coach, call and play better around him. He pointed to a stretch of roughly 18-20 minutes with no first downs and three straight three-and-outs, plus a turnover, as the reason the offense and run game never found rhythm. He defended Watson against the 'tentative' narrative, saying many throws weren't called or weren't executed. He explained Denzel Boston's lack of targets by the low snap count (about 49) and the lack of rhythm, and said it wasn't by design. Sampson is still being evaluated, with more info Wednesday, and another player (apparently Zion Johnson, per a garbled name) has no final update yet. Monken was very high on rookie linemen Austin Barber and Spencer Fano, said Barber will be starting, and said no personnel changes are expected in the secondary. He also praised the kick return game and punter Corey.

injuries.detail: Still being evaluated; Monken said more information will come Wednesday.
The transcript says 'Zyon', and the match to Zion Johnson is a best guess. Monken has no final update, but got good information Monday and will know more when he's back in the building Wednesday.

signals.claim: Watson will start at quarterback against Tampa Bay.
signals.note: The starting job is safe for now, but the offense around him struggled badly, so his fantasy value is shaky and depends on a fix to the operation and play-calling.
signals.quote: I anticipate Deshaun will be our starter.

signals.claim: Boston's low target total was due to limited snaps and lack of rhythm, not by design, and he should see more targets when the offense runs more plays.
signals.note: Boston had few targets in a 49-snap game, but Monken says it wasn't a role change and he expects more volume with a healthier game flow.
signals.quote: it wasn't by design. It certainly wasn't.

signals.claim: Sampson's availability will be clearer on Wednesday.
signals.note: The RB's status for Week 3 is uncertain, which affects backfield usage.
signals.quote: we're still evaluating Dylan, and we'll have more information on Wednesday.

signals.claim: Barber will be starting on the offensive line.
signals.note: A rookie lineman starting and developing is good news for protection and run-blocking stability.

signals.claim: Fano will continue to develop as a starter-caliber rookie lineman.
signals.note: Strong praise for a young OL piece that could help the line improve over the season.
signals.quote: Spencer's going to continue to grow.

signals.claim: The offense had a couple of good perimeter plays for Concepcion early in the game.
signals.note: He was a featured piece of the early perimeter plan, which is worth watching if the offense gets more plays.
signals.quote: We had a couple of good plays to, uh, to KC

topics.detail: Monken blamed slow huddle exits, play-call length, delay-of-game and timeout issues, and trying to do too much. He wants to shrink the calls and just get the play off.

The run game never got going because the offense had so few plays and a string of three-and-outs and turnovers. The first two runs went for about five yards each, but the offense never stacked plays to wear the defense down.

Jacksonville scored on six of seven first possessions. Monken said the run defense, pass defense and pass rush all failed, with some busted coverages in the back end. He thought open-field tackling was fine, but said Jacksonville's run schemes got to the second level easily.
Monken doesn't anticipate personnel changes in the secondary this week, including for the new cornerbacks.
Kick returns were a bright spot, including one by Rocket, but two holding penalties hurt. The punter, Corey, was praised for directional, high-hangtime kicks.
Monken expects Baker Mayfield to be highly competitive and ready in Tampa Bay's home opener. He rejected Mike Tomlin's 'Browns are the Browns' comment, calling the loss one bad week.
Monken said the QB decision isn't up for debate with players, and the team needs to support whoever is on the field.

title: Brian Schottenheimer: “Our Standards and Expectations Are High” | Press Conference
headline: Cowboys lose DeMarvion Overshown (hamstring, ~1-2 weeks) and Malik Hooker (fracture, ~2 weeks) for the DAL defense; Caleb Downs stays near the line, and Jaishawn Barham, Dee Winters and Shemar James get more linebacker snaps against Washington.
summary: Schottenheimer opened by confirming Malik Hooker has a fracture that should keep him out around two weeks, with surgery coming the next day. DeMarvion Overshown has a hamstring strain that could cost him 1-2 weeks, which the coach said is nothing long term. With Overshown out, Dee Winters is the most experienced linebacker, Jaishawn Barham got valuable snaps and will keep playing, Shemar James is valued, and Justin Barron and practice-squad veteran Curtis Robinson are options. Schottenheimer took blame for a flat opener, citing contain failures against Jaxson Dart, communication breakdowns, penalties (an Overshown out-of-bounds hit, a Javonte Williams taunting call) and missed run-game execution. He defended the fourth-and-inches punt decision, noting it was planned, and said he regrets the first play call and not adjusting sooner. He said Quinnen Williams and Kenny Clark played okay but not dominantly, and that Donovan Ezeiruaku had some beautiful rushes. He praised Caleb Downs and Cobie Durant but said Downs is best near the line of scrimmage, while P.J. Locke gave up a deep cross to the Giants' Likely. He expects padded practices and a physical week before Washington and Jayden Daniels, with Lamar Jackson coming a couple of weeks later. Offensively he said the line pass-protected well but had too much run-game penetration, and he wanted to run the ball better early.

title: Brian Schottenheimer: Postgame Week 1 #DALvsNYG
headline: Cowboys were pushed around in a 28-20 Week 1 loss to the Giants, and Malik Hooker may have a fractured forearm. The run game stalled and the defense was exposed on the edges and in the flat. Washington is up next.
summary: Schottenheimer said the Cowboys were poor in all three phases and that the Giants were the more physical team. Dallas's run game was stuffed, and he said Javonte Williams ran into a wall early because of too much penetration. The defense failed to contain Jaxson Dart on boots and gave up repeated dump-offs to running back Singletary, which he blamed on poor eyes and missed adjustments in match-zone coverage. He said the pass rush has to be better, since Dart looked comfortable. Dak Prescott's interception at the end of the first half led to a Giants score and a second-half score, which Schottenheimer called a double dip. He also cited nine penalties, including offside calls in short yardage and an unsportsmanlike penalty on Williams during a two-point attempt. He downplayed George Pickens' two first-half drops as early-season sloppiness. On injuries, Malik Hooker may have a fractured forearm, and a player who sounded like Overshown has a hamstring injury of unknown severity. He said he won't panic and that the team will regroup for a division game against Washington on Sunday at AT&T.

Hamstring injury of unknown severity. The caption rendered the name as 'Deimos', so the identification is not certain.

signals.note: His status for next week is unclear, and the identification rests on a garbled caption.

signals.claim: Williams was stuffed early because of heavy penetration, and the run game has to improve.
signals.note: The offensive line and run game struggled against the Giants' front, which lowers his short-term rushing outlook. The coach still called him one of the team's most dependable players.
signals.quote: That's not like Javonte.

signals.note: The coach isn't worried about the drops, so Pickens' target share should stay secure.

topics.detail: Dallas failed to contain Jaxson Dart on boots and kept giving up flat and check-down throws to Singletary. Schottenheimer blamed bad eyes in match-coverage zones and a lack of adjustments. He said the Giants were 4-for-4 in the red zone and 9-for-11 on third down.

Dallas had nine penalties, including offside calls in short yardage that gave the Giants free downs and extended drives. He said the team failed on discipline and on owning the line of scrimmage.

The Giants held the ball for roughly 36 minutes, which limited Dallas to few real possessions. The offense improved after halftime adjustments, and the Cowboys went for two late to cut the game to one score.

Schottenheimer told the first-time defensive play-caller not to flinch and said the loss is a lesson for the coaches. He said the young defenders need to learn faster, and that he doesn't want to live with this many mistakes.

title: Campbell on TNF vs. the Buffalo Bills
headline: Short week before TNF at Buffalo: OL Christian Mahogany is in doubt, Blake Miller is a bit more likely to play, Jahmyr Gibbs is expected to be fine, and the RB2 split behind him is still undecided.
summary: Campbell opened by praising Buffalo as an excellent, aggressive opponent. He singled out Josh Allen as their catalyst and the defensive line of Ed Oliver, Rossouw and Chubb, and he expects an electric Thursday-night atmosphere. The offensive line is banged up. Mahogany has a minor injury that is not long-term but may not clear by Thursday. Blake Miller is also a concern, and Campbell would rather bet on Miller playing than Mahogany, though he gave no firm answer and said more would be known Monday. He said the depth of Bartch, Juice Scruggs and Frazier is enough to get through, and he called Bartch's outing inconsistent and rusty but expects improvement. He called Sam LaPorta and the tight ends a huge part of the 160-yard rushing day, and praised LaPorta's work to get back from injury. He expects Gibbs to be recovered and ready after a heavy workload. The RB2 snap split is still being discussed, and Saylors needs to clean up pass protection after his biggest offensive workload. He praised Rock Ya-Sin for the game-ending two-point stop and said the defense expects Buffalo to push tempo, as New Orleans did late. He also said a player placed on IR (unnamed in the transcript) will be out a significant time.

title: Matt LaFleur: 'Can't have enough guys like Tucker Kraft'
headline: Tucker Kraft played 45 snaps in his return from injury and just got extended. Expect his workload to stay managed, but LaFleur wants to get him the ball downfield. Aaron Banks' availability for Week 2 is unclear, and the pass protection problems carry over.
summary: LaFleur reviewed the Week 1 loss to the Vikings and called the pass protection the main disappointment, citing several busts that should not happen and a quarterback hit about 15 times. He said the offense produced about ten explosive plays for 300-plus yards but finished only 1 of 4 in the red zone and kicked two field goals. He also pointed to pre-snap penalties (six, by his count: three false starts and three offsides) and mental errors as costly, and said the offsides problem from camp has not been fixed. He defended the fourth-and-one QB sneak decision and said Green Bay will stay aggressive on fourth-and-short. Tucker Kraft was capped at about 40 snaps but played 45, and LaFleur praised his conditioning and leadership after the Saturday extension. He said the team will look for ways to get Kraft the ball downfield, not just on checkdowns and screens. Aaron Banks' absence hurt the line's communication, and LaFleur called the line spots a competitive situation as the team looks for continuity. Jayden Reed had a third-and-25 pass hit off his hands, and an unnamed player (initials "WKS" in the captions) cramped late. A return from injury for "Micah" could come after Game 2, but the coach has not talked to the medical staff.

title: DeMeco Ryans Previews Texans vs Bengals Week 2 | Full Q&A
headline: David Montgomery scored three touchdowns in his Texans debut and Ryans praised his goal-line and tough-yardage work. LB Henry To'oTo'o (shoulder) is out for some time, and the defense faces an explosive Bengals offense after a Week 1 loss to Buffalo.
summary: Ryans was frustrated by the Week 1 loss to the Bills. He blamed 11-12 explosive plays allowed, about 12 missed tackles, no takeaways, and two Houston turnovers, including one on the first possession. He said the 2025 defense's reputation means nothing and the group has to earn it again this year. The offense drew praise: Montgomery scored three touchdowns in his debut, the line blocked well, and C.J. Stroud had clean pockets and made good decisions. Every skill player touched the ball, and Ryans singled out the contested catches. Newcomer Kayshon Boutte made an explosive play despite arriving late, and Ryans said he's being moved around the formation. On injuries, To'oTo'o has a shoulder injury and will be out for some time, with no IR decision yet. A linebacker whose name the captions garbled (likely Jake Hansen) has a groin injury and is week to week. Special teams earned praise for the punter and a 58-yard field goal, but kick coverage and the return game left yards on the field. Next up is Cincinnati, with Burrow, Chase and Higgins, which Ryans called another test against explosive plays.

title: Shane Steichen: Week 1 Recap, Colts vs. Ravens
headline: Steichen called the Week 1 loss extremely disappointing in all three phases. Alec Pierce's hand/wrist is fine, and rookie CJ Allen dressed but didn't play and has no timeline for a bigger role.

He said the defensive pre-snap confusion is a team-wide issue, not just about Kim wearing the headset for the first time. He called the blitz-pickup problems correctable and said he has a ton of confidence in Tony and the protection schemes. He took some responsibility for the offense stalling against heavy pressure, saying he has to call things better and get players into open spots against the blitz. title: Coen Reflects on Performance in Week 1 Win, Fast Start & High-Level Play | Press Conference
headline: Coen expects WR Brian Thomas Jr. to 'probably' be active vs. Denver on Monday night, praised Tuten's running and Strange's red-zone involvement, and said TE Nate Boerkircher is taking over the hard downs.

He said he told the staff to get Brenton Strange going, and Strange then scored a touchdown. Bhayshul Tuten ran hard and through arm tackles, though he needs to be more patient in the open field. Trevor Lawrence's off-schedule scrambling was a highlight, especially a touchdown to Josh Cameron on the exact play they ran in the Carolina joint practice. Rookie OL Emmanuel Pregnon was praised for his pass protection in his first start, and Ventrell Miller was active in his first start on defense. title: Head Coach Jim Harbaugh Postgame Press Conference vs. Cardinals
headline: Chargers lost Week 1 to the Cardinals in a sloppy game, and Ladd McConkey's injury status is unresolved, with the coach offering no update beyond what was already released.
summary: Harbaugh called the loss a start the team didn't want and gave Arizona credit. He called the team's play sloppy, pointing mostly to penalties, false starts and misalignments, and said penalties were a big factor in the second half. He liked the opening drive, which went from the 11-yard line to the Arizona 3 without points, and said it showed what the offense can do. Another good drive ended in a turnover, and neither team punted in the first half. He defended going for it on fourth down at the 3 late in the second quarter, saying he wanted seven points rather than a field goal and a short field for Arizona. The defense needs more stops, and he said they gave up too many first downs. He mentioned a twist on the blocked punt and said special teams needs better coaching, practice and execution. He gave no further update on Ladd McConkey. He said the team would bounce back and expects resolve from its competitors. Asked about a rotation involving two players (the names are garbled in the captions) he said it was the best thing to win, and that they would look at whether it continues.

title: Kellen Moore recaps overtime loss vs. Lions 9/14/2026
headline: Kamara, Cam Jordan and Oscar Delp (all missed Week 1) are 'progressing well' with Week 2 status TBD; Bryce Lance and CJ Donaldson earned real offensive roles in the OT loss to Detroit.
summary: Moore said the Saints came out of the overtime loss to Detroit fairly clean medically. Cam Jordan, Alvin Kamara and Oscar Delp, who were unavailable, are all progressing well and will be judged as the week goes on. He called the game a back-and-forth battle the team had chances to win, and said the focus now is on self-improvement ahead of a road game at Baltimore. The run game did not get going the way he wanted against a good run-stopping Lions team, and falling behind 21-0 at one point cut down the run opportunities before the game settled into more balanced play in the fourth quarter. He praised Travis Etienne's hard running and red-zone third-down catch, Noah Fant's catches and physicality as a blocker, and rookie Bryce Lance's heavy snap count, fourth-down catch and reliability. Barion Brown handled returns, got a few offensive snaps, and will keep that role. CJ Donaldson played about 15 snaps with a third-down protection and short-yardage package, and Moore was happy with how he earned it. On defense, Moore said the run fits, gap integrity and communication need to improve after Jahmyr Gibbs had a big game. He described the linebacker and corner rotations (Danny Stutsman/Pete Werner, Martin Emerson/Quincy Riley) as largely pre-planned, with Mason Murphy also earning opportunities. He said Kamara will be part of the offense 'shortly'.

title: Coach John Harbaugh: 'Everything you do before is a foundation for what you're going to do next'
headline: Skattebo drove a dominant ground game and Dart was accurate and efficient (7-of-7 on third down per a reporter), but Harbaugh stressed ball security after four fumbles.
summary: Harbaugh opened by crediting the run game's success to Cam Skattebo, who ran hard, set the tempo and read his blocks well, along with good blocking and a solid game plan. He added that plenty still needs to improve. On Jaxson Dart, he singled out accuracy and on-time rhythm throws, especially in critical situations against both man and zone. He called the third-down efficiency exactly what you hope for and said it moves the chains. He said the defense's personnel lets them slide edge rushers like Kayvon Thibodeaux inside, which makes twists and stunts more effective. He said Thibodeaux is excited about the role. On the secondary, he called a couple of the pass interference calls justified and one or maybe two gray, and he would not explain the cornerback substitutions beyond wanting the best combination. He praised fullback Patrick Ricard as unique and built into the offense's identity. He called ball security a non-negotiable and said putting the ball on the ground four times is unacceptable. Asked about health coming out of the game, he said only 'Fine.' He stressed that last night's performance won't be good enough next Monday night.

Also exited during the game, and Colton Hood replaced him. No specific injury update was given.

signals.note: The coach's first credit for the successful ground game went to Skattebo, which supports his lead-back workload and efficiency.

signals.note: Harbaugh praised his accuracy, timing and third-down efficiency, which bodes well for passing-game consistency.
signals.quote: I thought his accuracy was really good

signals.note: The interior rush role creates free-rusher chances, which helps his sack and pressure upside in IDP formats.

title: Aaron Glenn Press Conference (9/14)
headline: Jets open 1-0 with a balanced offense and Geno Smith hitting deep shots, but Minkah Fitzpatrick (groin) and Omar Cooper Jr. (ankle) are being evaluated, with updates due this afternoon.
summary: Glenn opened by thanking the traveling Jets fans and praised the team for creating its own momentum in a week one win. He liked the balance and efficiency on offense, called the O-line outstanding for giving Geno Smith time on explosive downfield plays, and said the defense harassed the quarterback and disrupted receivers. He wants to fix offensive penalties and settling for field goals on three trips in scoring position. On defense he flagged problems leveraging the ball and a late touchdown that kept the game from being sealed. Minkah Fitzpatrick (groin) and Omar Cooper Jr. (ankle) are both awaiting evaluation results, with more information expected this afternoon. Dane Belton stepped in for Fitzpatrick and played safety and nickel, and when Jarvis Brownlee went down Belton moved to nickel while Andre Cisco played safety. Glenn said Geno threw at close to 80%, with growing trust between him and the skill players, including Garrett Wilson. He called the tight end room (Kenyon Sadiq, Mason Taylor, Jeremy Ruckert, Jelani Woods) a weapon that allows 12 and 13 personnel, and said they will keep adding to its workload. He also praised Demario Davis as a smart, disruptive player and leader.

title: Nick Sirianni Press Conference: September 14, 2026
headline: Sirianni says the target distribution will vary week to week, and he backed Goedert, Hurts, Saquon Barkley as the lead back, and Makai Lemon. He also vowed to get Marquise Brown more involved after Brown was shut out of reps.
summary: After the Sunday night win over Washington, Sirianni said the offensive line gave up some pressures but also got good movement, and he framed the pressures as an issue for the whole offense rather than one spot. He praised Dallas Goedert for being consistent and for showing different parts of his game: over-the-middle catches, yards after the catch, red zone work and some outside alignments. He called Jalen Hurts' handling of new elements, such as seven-step drops from under center, a nice job and said the team wouldn't have installed them otherwise. On the run game, he defended the commitment to it and the explosive 46-yard gain that set up a touchdown. He said Saquon Barkley is the lead guy, and that Will Shipley and Tank Bigsby are trusted, with Shipley's carries partly a product of tempo and sub rules. He said Marquise Brown was shut out of reps due to rotations but that the team wants him in the game and will make a better effort next time. He also said Landon Dickerson's power is a strength despite the pressures he gave up, and that Makai Lemon contributes in ways that don't show up in stats. Asked about the evenly spread targets, he said every game differs and the hot hand gets fed, singling out DeVonta Smith, Goedert and a camp standout he called Tay.

title: WATCH: The Mike McCarthy Press Conference Show presented by PNC (Week 2 at Patriots)
headline: Steelers beat Atlanta 20-13 and head to New England. T.J. Watt is on a ~40-snap plan and Cam Heyward was a standout. Joey Porter Jr. is still ramping up with no firm return date, and the run game needs more volume.
summary: McCarthy said the win was important but the bigger goal was setting a standard of play, and he praised the defense for carrying the team. He criticized the offense's third-down conversions (3 of 13), poor ball security, and some missed deep shots. He called his own play calling "herky jerky" and said he didn't get the offense into a rhythm. He said he was happy with the four-minute offense and thought the run game needed about ten more attempts. He defended the passing design by saying the middle of the field is the fastest way to the end zone and that Atlanta played a lot of one-high. He raved about Cam Heyward's three batted passes and T.J. Watt's impact, and said Watt was projected for about 40 snaps under his play-time projection plan. Alex Highsmith was put in the same category as Heyward. He singled out Michael Pittman as having made the most of his opportunities and said some receivers got more chances than others. On Joey Porter Jr., he said holding him out was his own decision, the hope is for more work Wednesday, and he expects Porter to play once the ramp-up ends. He declined to say more about the contract situation. Next up is a road game at New England, where he expects a balanced Patriots attack.

signals.quote: he's clearly was the most impactful player in that game.

signals.note: McCarthy praised his three batted passes and pre-snap recognition, which is good for IDP value despite a managed snap count.
signals.quote: I thought he had a hell of a game.

signals.note: The split is meant to keep both backs fresh, so neither is likely to dominate touches. McCarthy said the run game needed about ten more attempts.

McCarthy said the defense drew a "line in the sand" and carried the team, with a rotated defensive line and Watt's snaps managed by design through a play-time projection report.
McCarthy said the business component is an individual matter for each player, declined to say it would become a distraction, and said he had already talked about it more than ever.

McCarthy expects New England to stay balanced on offense, as Josh McDaniels has done, and said the way Pittsburgh lines up will influence their approach. He framed the game as a chance to win the first road game.

title: Todd Bowles on Bucs vs. Bengals: Josiah Trotter's Impact | Press Conference
headline: Bucs lost Week 1 to Cincinnati despite 27 points, with turnovers (Baker Mayfield, Bucky Irving) the main concern; Parrish has a back sprain with negative imaging, Trotter made an impact, and Egbuka is still working his way back.
summary: Bowles said Jacob Parrish has a back sprain; X-ray and MRI were negative, so it's a matter of soreness subsiding. Benjamin Morrison played very well after stepping in, covering and tackling without missing a beat. The pass rush was poor because the linemen played as individuals rather than together, and Rueben Bain took a mental step back while Yaya Diaby played hard. Turnovers were the dominant theme: Mayfield must protect the ball and know when to go down, and Irving must secure it with two hands even though he ran sharply. Bowles declined to judge Zac Robinson's first game as play-caller on one game, saying the offense scored 27 and can be effective. Alex Anzalone's man coverage was fine, but he blew two zone drops, missed tackles, and was rusty. Godwin, Egbuka and Ted Hurst III all played fast/hard, with Egbuka still working back from missed time. Bowles said Bain's conditioning was fine but his hand placement was rusty, and that he should improve with more practice time. Next up is Cleveland, where Bowles dismissed concerns about Mayfield pressing against his former team.

title: Robert Saleh Press Conference | Tennessee Titans
headline: Cedric Gray (concussion) expected back Week 2 vs. PHI; Cam Ward's struggles pinned on protection and execution; Carnell Tate had a good debut and Saleh wants him to get more targets.
summary: Saleh opened by taking accountability for a poor Week 1 loss to the Jets in all three phases. He credited New York for running the ball 40 times, and said Tennessee's second-half shift to chasing tackles for loss produced explosive pass plays. The offense missed early first-down runs and couldn't stay ahead of the chains, which cut the rushing attempts to 14. On Cam Ward, he said production has to be better, but he praised his improved pocket presence and extended drives on the first series. He blamed the lack of deep shots on pass protection collapsing and on receivers needing to make plays, and he pointed to Ward's seven coordinators in seven years as a reason to be patient. He was positive on rookie linebacker Anthony Hill, who flew around and made a lot of tackles in place of Cedric Gray. Gray appears to have cleared concussion protocol and Saleh believes he's good for Week 2, though he wanted to double-check. Saleh also liked rookie WR Carnell Tate's first game, calling it his best performance of the preseason and regular season combined, and said he hopes to get him more chances to touch the ball. Next up is Philadelphia, and he said the specific fixes would be set on Wednesday.

The Jets kept the passing game underneath and pressure collapsed quickly on deep shots, so Ward couldn't take shots downfield. Saleh also mentioned route-angle and timing issues between Ward and the rookie receiver.

title: HC Dan Quinn | 09/13/26
headline: Quinn praised Jayden Daniels' return and said Stefon Diggs and Terry McLaurin both stayed locked in. WAS lost a division game to Philadelphia on miscues, and no injury updates yet even though a couple of players left the game.
summary: Quinn called the division loss to Philadelphia a painful one. He liked the team's fight but said miscues, pre-snap penalties and explosive plays allowed (including a Jalen Hurts scramble and a Saquon Barkley run) cost them. He called Jayden Daniels' return significant and said Daniels is still learning lessons from 2025, such as throwing the ball away. He praised Stefon Diggs' competitiveness, said he talked with him about a late penalty, and noted the offense improved as the game went on by marrying the run and pass games. On the two-point try, a shovel pass with a flat option to Rachaad White, he said the play was well designed and practiced but was blown up by penetration. He said Terry McLaurin got touches late and stayed focused, since Philadelphia clouded coverage to take him away, and that the offense has to find other open spots. On injuries, he said a couple of players did not finish the game but he had nothing to share yet and would update next time.

injuries.detail: Quinn said a couple of players did not finish the game but gave no names or details, and promised an update at the next press conference.

signals.claim: Daniels is back as the starting QB and is learning from 2025, such as throwing the ball away rather than forcing plays.
signals.note: Daniels is healthy and trusted as a competitor, which supports his fantasy outlook.
signals.quote: it's great to have Jayden back. I thought that was significant.

signals.claim: Diggs will remain a competitive presence in the offense, with the passing game improving as it balances with the run.
signals.note: Quinn praised his fight but gave no target-share specifics, and a penalty after a touchdown drew a talking-to.
signals.quote: I love the competitive nature that he brings to our team.

signals.claim: Opponents will keep trying to take McLaurin away with coverage, so targets may come in bursts and the offense must find other options.
signals.note: He was quiet until late because Philadelphia clouded him, which makes his target volume matchup-dependent.
signals.quote: when his moments came to go get some, he did.

signals.claim: White was the flat option on the shovel pass for the two-point try, which was blown up by penetration.
signals.note: He has a role in red-zone and goal-line packages, but the play itself failed.

topics.detail: Quinn was frustrated by the pre-snap penalties, including a false start. He said the team was prepared for the crowd noise and he wants answers from officials.
Quinn liked the speed, hitting and physicality, but wants to eliminate explosive plays and third-and-long scrambles. He singled out Hurts' 22-yard scramble and Barkley's elusiveness.

The offense improved as the game went on, and Quinn said sticking with the run mattered. He said both play-callers were prepared and that he communicates fourth-down and two-point decisions with them during the week.
Quinn said the team goes right back into another division game and wants to apply this week's lessons across all three phases.
